chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Saif ibn 'Umayrah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave who slandered a free man. He said: 'He is flogged with eighty [strikes]. This is from the rights of the Muslims.' Then he said: 'As for what is from the rights of Allah, the Exalted, then he is struck with half the punishment.' I said: 'What is that which is from the rights of Allah?' He said: 'When he commits adultery or drinks wine, this is from the rights in which half the punishment is struck.'

key_terms.حُرّاً: Free man (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.قَذَفَ: Slandered (specifically in the context of hadd al-judud)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the punishment for a slave slandering a free man versus committing adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify the distinction between *hadd* punishments for slaves versus free men, specifically noting that while slander against a free man carries the full eighty lashes as a communal right (*haqq al-nas*), sexual misconduct or wine drinking incurs only half the standard penalty as a divine right (*haqq Allah*). This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that slaves, due to their partial legal capacity, receive reduced corporal punishment for sins against God, whereas their liability for interpersonal wrongs remains comparable to free individuals.
